main_text.p: diriperentur etiam fortissima mœnia. Sint igitur urbes, quam oppugnabit, ad cœlum usque sublimes, & munitiones tam loci naturâ, quam artis industriâ firmissimæ: ille suis viribus longè inferiores existimabit; & frustra erit carnalis fiducia, quæ ab his sine Deo, & contra ejus decretum, defensionem exspectat.

§. 4. Sequentia in textu originali verbis præteriti temporis affirmantur: unde vau copula hic exercet potestatem conjunctionis temporalis, quod plurics[?] locum habere indicant Philologi. Colligere pulverem phrasis est, quæ terræ notat aggestionem, unde munimenta oppugnabant veteres. Conf. 2 Sam. 20: 25. 2 Reg. 19: 32. Jef. 29: 3. 37: 3. Ezech. 4: 2. Dan. 11: 15. Ejus consequens est capere seu occupare eam. Præteritum ita subjunctive acceptum, notat hic tempus, quandò ita rideret quodcunque munimentum: sc. à quo exemplo esset[?] edoctus, ut fortissimam capere urbem valuerit. Forte clanculum indigitat certam aliquam civitatem, à cujus occupatione sibi talem armorum suc-cessum sponderet: quo in casu ego hic respici Ninives occupationem censerem, quæ fuit monarchiæ Assyriacæ munitissima metropolis, à cujus debellatione videbatur nihil superesse, quod non facile superare posset ejus victor.

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "plurics" (possibly "pluries") and "esset" (printed with a diacritic-like mark) are marked [?]. The printed verse heading has a stray double comma after "luet", rendered as a single comma. The printed letter "v" in "pervaserit" is a rounded form, transcribed as v. An ornament (dot-and-star) between the second paragraph and the verse heading is not text and is omitted. The catchword "com-" is the first syllable of the next page's opening word.
